title: Floating combat text: Terraria colours, pop-in, constant screen size, green heal and blue mana numbers
player_outcome: Hits pop in with a quick bounce: orange normal hits, bigger red-orange crits, pink-red when you get hurt. Drinking a potion floats a green '+50' over your head, and mana potions a blue one. Numbers stay the same size on screen at any distance, as in 2D Terraria.
design: Core feedback event: new partial src/Strata.Core/Session/GameWorld.Feedback.cs with `event Action<PlayerEntity, int, bool>? PlayerHealed` (amount, mana) and `ReportHeal(p, amount, mana)`. Vitals.Heal and RestoreMana return the amount actually applied (int instead of void; existing callers ignore it).

Raise PlayerHealed from:
- ItemUseSystem.Consume. Move Consume into a new partial ItemUseSystem.Consume.cs first, since ItemUseSystem.cs is at 375 lines.
- Life steal in NpcSystem.Hit (NpcSystem.cs:291).
- TownCommerce.Heal (the nurse).

Heart and mana-star pickups (feel phase) call ReportHeal too.

Rewrite CombatEffects.Number:
- Kinds: Hostile Color8(255,160,80); Crit Color8(255,100,30) at ×1.25 with ±0.05 m x-jitter; ToPlayer Color8(255,80,90); HealLife (100,255,100); HealMana (100,100,255).
- Label3D FixedSize = true, PixelSize ≈ 0.0011 (tune on screenshots), font UiFonts.Bold, outline 12.
- Pop: Scale 0.3 → 1 over 0.08 s (TransitionType.Back).
- Rise with decaying speed 0.9 m over 0.9 s; fade starts at 0.4 s.
- Heal numbers appear at head + 0.4 m in third person, and at eye + Aim·1.2 + 0.3 m up in first person.
Pool cap by graphics preset (low 24, medium 48, high/ultra 80); when exhausted, recycle the oldest label. No per-number allocation after warm-up.
files_modify: game/Entities/CombatEffects.cs — colours, pop, fixed size, heal numbers, pool cap
tests: CombatPlayerTests: DrinkingAPotionReportsTheHealedAmount (60/100 life + lesser healing potion → event with 40); ManaPotionReportsMana; FullLifeReportsNothing
verification: dotnet test; smoke combat.cmds and ui.cmds pass
Lavapipe exec: spawn a slime, swing, screenshot during the pop; compare sizes near and far
risks: The feel phase edits CombatEffects (death puffs, blood, hit dust); this WP changes only Number, NewLabel and the pool. Coordinate on the file.
P3 also edits ItemUseSystem; the partial split reduces the conflict surface.
